value.body: A community health nurse provides nursing care and health education outside hospitals: in villages and urban wards, public health programmes, schools and patients' homes. Employers include state health departments under the National Health Mission, primary health facilities, NGOs and home-care services. Days involve health screening, immunisation and mother-and-child follow-up, chronic disease checks and home visits.

items.note: Community health nursing is part of the course

items.value: Community Health Officer (CHO) at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
items.note: Usually B.Sc Nursing plus a certificate or bridge course in community health

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After a B.Sc Nursing and State Nursing Council registration, freshers apply to state National Health Mission recruitment for CHO and programme posts, or join NGOs and home-care services. CHO posts usually need the community health certificate, which some states provide after selection.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Health screening and first-level care in the community
Health education for families and groups
Record-keeping on health programme apps and registers
Home care such as wound care and post-discharge follow-up

value.title: At a glance
items: Many National Health Mission posts are contractual, with terms set by each state.
Postings are often in rural or remote areas.
Next steps include public health supervisor roles, an M.Sc Nursing (Community Health) or an MPH.
